I like this game. It's a good game compared to where it was multiple years ago but there are still so many issues with the game, and some of that has come from it being worked on for so long. 

Nothing in this game is fully fleshed out. There are a lot of things that are tried, and to a various degree even succeed at keeping me engaged for a while. Most of the game mechanics are like this for about 2 hours, then you kinda top out and get bored. Let's rapid fire through game mecahnics that aren't fully fleshed out. 

Units are the worst. Either you are a slave to the navigation maps that provide almost no units, you do some trade system stuff that doesn't make that many units, you can have an S tier settlement to make almost no units, or you can just scan stuff through a visor after eating a magic donut and you make billions per hour. 
Nanites? By far the best way to make nanites is to farm mold. Is it fun? no. but if you want to progress at anything other than a snails pace, you don't have many options that are fun.
the fix: nerf mold farming, make the best way to get nanites to be exploring the galaxy. the nanites you get from discovering creatures and fauna just needs a small buff to be more viable, and raiding outposts needs to be harder but more rewarding.

Settlements is a big pain point for me as they have so much potential but are completely left to dry in so many ways. When you get an S tier settlement you have options of what gets produced for you, but since units don't matter unless you are exploiting mechanics, it's almost worthless. It provides no other real benefit for all the time you put in. 

Combat is good until you realize when you are fighting a pirate dreadnought for the first time thinking "this will be what the combat is like in this game?" then you warp to another system, get that same fight again, realize it's the same fight again. And once you have good modules it's just over for anybody you see.

Corvettes are cool. I spent a lot of time to make a pretty good one. I'll give hello games that but even that system isn't fully fleshed out. 

The main mission is just a bunch of fetch quests with dialog about being alone, and honestly I think the game would be better without a main story at all or the option to skip it. 

Your characters movement is horrible, you bump into everything that is tiny and it makes your camera move pretty violently if you are clipping, the quests make me upset because there are permanent side quests that you cannot get out of the "side quest" page. 

If you take every major update, you see that this game has "transformed into something new" and that's true, it has, but it's also a mess that needs to be cleaned up. it's overwhelming at first when you learn there is a whole cooking system put in the game, but once you get a few pretty basic ingredients you can cook almost anything in the game. 

I hope the next few updates for a while calm down the new features and expand on the existing ones. 

Thank you for still working on the game Hello Games.

I'm trying to figure out why I don't like No Man’s Sky. I find this game boring. Which surprises me, since in other games I like the core gameplay loop: the locust. The locust can be described as taking anything that isn’t nailed to the floor. So why can I sink hundreds of hours into games like Starfield or The Last Caretaker, but I zone out after only 25 in No Man’s Sky?

I think the answer is context. No Man’s Sky doesn’t give me anything to care about. There is a story, but it’s told in such a way that I can’t be bothered to engage with it. 

You are dropped on a random planet, and go figure it out. And in the first few hours, I had my fun, but then I asked myself a very obvious question: Why am I doing any of it? In a normal game, I would have narrative to lean on, or interesting characters, set pieces, or visuals. But this game doesn’t really have any. Any interesting visual will get drowned out by how many times it occurs, and it will happen on all the planets you will visit. All (well, almost all) characters are procedurally generated, and those that aren’t might as well be. And narrative, while it exists, is told in such a way that I didn’t care.

And without anything else to lean on, the locust is just a chore. Gather more resources to go to the next planet. Will there be anything interesting there? Probably turns to no, and no turns to I don’t care. Will we do anything interesting there? We will gather more resources…

Developers added more content over the years and ironed out multiple rough edges. But the gameplay loop is boring. If the primary gameplay loop is boring, I won’t be motivated to engage with the other loops. And guess what? I was bored.

I read online that this game is a sandbox, and I need to remind people: the game doesn’t promise that anywhere on its Steam page. It explicitly names “exploration” and “survival”. And exploration sucks, mainly because of repetition, and survival is just meh. 

Also, the UI is bad; I don’t understand how a 10-year-old game can have UI that sucks. You would think that it's one of the first things developers would fix first. But apparently the UI in the original game sucked even more.

Would I recommend this game? For the current price: fuck no. With a big enough discount? Only if you treat this game as a sandbox and can find your own fun. Personally, when I pay for entertainment, I'd rather games be more structured than “find your own fun.”

It's a midpoint between three genres:
1. Terrain and environment building/resource extraction (minecraft, valheim)
2. Exploration and tech progression (subnautica, Ark)
3. Space sim (elite dangerous, space engineers)
It does some of everything but not as good as the other, more focused games above. 

You might like it a lot. But I can't make myself go back to it for several reasons:
- Nothing you can gain is particularly appealing, visually. The design style seems to be going for a Star Wars-esque aesthetic (your starting ship is reminiscent of an X-wing, your exosuit is similar to a rebel pilot outfit, etc.) but it just doesn't hit the mark. Everything is so BUSY, like the art director thinks the final step to looking cool is vomiting a bunch of flaps, bumps and angles onto every surface.
- Progression is VERY sluggish. What accounts for the extended tutorial is well over 2 hours and I still feel the leash holding me back. Why do I need ancient blueprints to unlock commonplace technology? Why are storage crates locked behind >12 hours' worth of missions, story or otherwise? Holy shit, get to the point.
- Resource gathering is unfun. The game revolves around mining and such but getting to, harvesting, and storing material is tedious. And you can only build ten crates! In the entire game! Bases share the same storage space, the chests just access those spaces.
- The game is presented as a space combat simulator, but the primary gameplay loop is resource extraction. Four hours in and I don't have any idea when the fighting - when the FUN - begins to start.

I genuinely wanted to like this game. I hope everyone who purchases is has fun. I know that the developers are good dudes that want to make a good product, but nothing about it comes close to bringing me back.

Such a great experience!
I knew of the game since it was announced, and was very hyped for it, even though i knew it would have never ran on my than old shitty laptop.
I was very sad when it came out to be a flop at launch.
Many years passed and i was reminded of it this year.
I bought it to play it as a coop survival with a friend, we played for 2 hours and ran out of time.
After some months i decided to start a new save by myself, and oh boy did i catch the bug.
I managed to put in 50+ hours in 2 weeks.
The game is great, the feeling of vastness and will to explore is incredible.
I often get lost doing a hundred things at once. I have to set strict goals for every play session, otherwise i end up spending 4 hours and completing nothing.
The progress is great, the learning curve is damn bloody satisfying and engaging.
The many worlds feel unique and great even after encountering similar planets multiple times.
I feel more than anything, this is an exploration game, and man it delivers. I have not been this engaged with a game in many years. It truly delivers a great scratch for that ich of wondering the universe in fancy unique ships and carving a path of your own choice trough the galaxy.
Great alone, great with randoms, great with friends.
The community is amazing also.

I could blabber endlessly about the game, but lets get more focused.
Graphics are good, the art style is what shines, and flying over a gorgeous world with 2 rainbows in the sky and another planned in the background never gets old.
Gameplay is fantastic, there are tens if not hundreds of things to do and focus on, and the main systems are basic enough to be understood and yet diverse enough to enjoy for a long time.
Combat is fine, could be more in depth, but for what it is and the plenty encounters the game offers, its fine.
The environment is great, planet landscapes, systems and galaxies are all procedurally generated. While planet exploration could get a bit stale because of the repetitive landscape, it still offers decent engagement trough different biomes. Some planets are just way more amazing than others.
The jobs/missions you get to do are great.
The economy system is simple yet fun and satisfying.
The base/ship building, oh man, its fantastic.
The story quests and world lore that you uncover by just talking to random npcs us awesome.

Overall, this game is an experience, and a damn good one at that.
If you are in the mood to explore endless worlds, build ships, travel trough space and waste a lot of time doing it (also you like minimal guidance, and great freedome), this is the game for you.
Similar to Cyberpunk 2077, a rough start, that lead to polished jewel.
This game made my life better and took me back to my childhood days when i was hyped to come home and jump in a great game, when worries and life was locked far away, and i immersed myself in a great fictional world.

No Man's Sky is one of the best video games ever made. Most people have heard about its rocky start but Hello Games stuck with it, relentlessly pursuing their vision and beyond. For years now it has been a masterpiece that just keeps getting better. There is so much to do in this game and so much personal creativity you can express. It's largely a sandbox game but with some directed goals here and there where you can put your focus if you like. The visuals are often quite stunning and you strongly feel drawn into the universe of No Man's Sky. 

The experience elevates to a whole other level if you play the game in VR. That VR experience of hopping in a spaceship and flying into space, or walking the corridors of your corvette, or plundering a haunted derelict freighter in space all from the perspective of "being there" is incredible. The VR experience isn't intensely kinetic. You won't be doing manual reloads on your weapon or scaling walls with your hands. in fact, I play the game seated. Yet it is extremely immersive and there are plenty of little touches that make the VR experience come home, such as grabbing the cockpit hatch and lifting it to leave your spaceship. Also, for a game with a lot of moving parts the controls are very well done.

No Man's Sky is largely a chill and relaxing game. Fights with the Sentinels can be intense. Pirate freighter battles are frenetic and not entirely simple to win. Much of the game, however, is about exploration, harvesting resources, improving your gear, and building functional & appealing bases, corvettes, and space platforms. There's even some light management sim elements in dealing with Settlements.

The bottom line is that this is a great game for anyone, but especially for those who like sci-fi, exploration, sandbox games, or who want to lose themselves in another place and have the feeling that they can go anywhere and do nearly anything. When a game is still pulling in brand new players ten years after release, its clear that the experience is something special.

There could also be alien encounters where the ships are derelict, but in a style where it's like those start stations you can visit to sell/buy tool and ship equipment and it's like Mass Effect / Doom themed interiors with some massive grimdark possible freighters and the combat can be like as now the game is with some possible entering into a megalophobia space creature as big or bigger than the start station.

Personally I need a bit of direction in a game. No Man's Sky is unfortunately not that. Subnautica had a decent progression to it though while this felt a bit empty.
